title: Wave-Particle Duality
text: Wave-particle duality is the concept in quantum mechanics that every particle or quantum entity exhibits both wave and particle properties. This duality was demonstrated by the famous double-slit experiment, in which electrons fired at a barrier with two slits create an interference pattern characteristic of waves, even when fired one at a time. The wave nature of particles is described by a probability wave function, while particle nature is observed upon measurement. Louis de Broglie proposed in 1924 that all matter has an associated wavelength inversely proportional to its momentum. This duality is a central feature of quantum mechanics that has no classical equivalent.
